conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’ll be guiding you through the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS. It’s a brief, well-studied questionnaire that helps us understand how moms are feeling emotionally in the first weeks and months after birth.  

Everything you share stays confidential within our care team, and there’s no right or wrong answer—just whatever is true for you. We’ll go through ten questions about how you’ve felt over the past seven days; each one usually only takes a moment to answer.  

Whenever you’re ready, we can begin.  

To start: Over the past seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult lately?
I can still laugh sometimes—like when my sister sent me that silly video yesterday—but I do notice it takes more effort. Things that used to crack me up right away feel kind of muted now.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Sometimes, yes, but it’s definitely harder than it used to be.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things
I still get little sparks of excitement—like when I think about taking the baby for his check-up—but they fade fast. Mostly I’m just tired and hoping I’ll feel like myself again soon.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a couple of times this week. Like when he wouldn’t settle after his midnight feed, I kept thinking maybe I’m not burping him right or I ate something that bothered him. Rationally I know babies just fuss, but the thought still pops in that I must’ve messed up somehow.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

A few nights I’ve lain in bed with my heart racing, sure something tiny—like a hiccup or a funny breathing sound—means he’s sick, even though he’s fine. Nothing huge, but the worry just shows up and hangs around longer than it should.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Not full-on panic, but sometimes, like when the house is quiet and I’m finally alone with him, this sudden knot of fear hits—like I’m not safe or something bad’s about to happen. It passes after a minute, but it’s unsettling.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days I manage—get the bottles washed, fold the tiny laundry—but by late afternoon it feels like the to-do pile is taller than I am. I’ll rock him with one foot while scrolling “how to soothe a fussy baby” articles and think, “I can’t keep all these plates spinning.” So yeah, sometimes it feels like I’m barely treading water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

I wouldn’t call it “so unhappy,” but I do stare at the ceiling a lot after his 3 a.m. feed. My mind just keeps looping—did I swaddle him tight enough, will he wake again in an hour—so it takes forever to drift back off, even though I’m exhausted.
I have felt sad or miserable
I get waves of that a few times a week. Yesterday I cried a little when I couldn’t get him to latch—nothing major, just this heavy “blah” feeling that sits on my chest for a while and then lifts.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Not “so unhappy” that I can’t stop—I’ve only teared up twice this week. Once when the diaper leaked all over the last clean outfit at 2 a.m., and once when my mom left after visiting. It’s more like the tears just slip out before I realize I’m feeling low.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, never. I’m tired and overwhelmed sometimes, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 16: **Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note**

**Identified Symptoms / Concerns**  
- Anhedonia: diminished ability to enjoy activities; pleasure “fades fast”  
- Low mood: episodic sadness, “heavy blah feeling” several times per week  
- Tearfulness: twice this week under minor stressors  
- Excessive guilt / self-blame re infant care (“must’ve messed up”)  
- Unwarranted anxiety about infant health, heart racing, intrusive worry  
- Brief fear/panic episodes with no clear trigger, resolves in minutes  
- Subjective overwhelm: feels tasks “taller than I am,” difficulty coping by late afternoon  
- Sleep disruption: difficulty returning to sleep after night feeds related to looping worries  
- Fatigue and hope to “feel like myself again”

**Pattern Summary**  
Persistent low mood with anhedonia, frequent guilt, and anxiety dominate the clinical picture; functional impact evident in coping and sleep. No self-harm ideation reported.

**Screening Significance**  
Meets partial clinical threshold for probable **postpartum depression** with prominent **anxiety features**; further evaluation recommended to rule out Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset and/or Postpartum Anxiety Disorder.

**Risk Factors Present**  
- ≥ 2-week duration of mood and anxiety symptoms  
- Sleep impairment tied to mood/worry  
- Feelings of inadequacy and guilt  
- Overwhelm impacting daily functioning  
- Absence of suicidal ideation (documented)

**Plan**  
Provide education, supportive listening, and arrange formal assessment (PHQ-9, GAD-7, EPDS) at next contact; consider expedited referral to perinatal mental health specialty if symptoms persist or worsen.
